chain.label: Degraded/doubtful deceleration capability (No. 1 thrust reverser inoperative, autobrake write-ups)
chain.trigger: the airplane was dispatched to ANC with the No. 1 (left engine) thrust reverser inoperative; maintenance logs contained three write-ups about instances in which the autobrakes failed to arm at takeoff or failed to function properly on landing

chain.label: Crew lacked operational proficiency with the airport performance laptop computer (APLC)
chain.trigger: two pilots with significant APLC experience at FedEx failed to properly interpret the calculated landing distances... other experienced flight crews may also be deficient in their operational knowledge of how APLC systems function

chain.label: Crew misinterpreted APLC landing distance data, computing a 780-foot stopping margin instead of 1,680 feet
chain.trigger: the flight crew misinterpreted the APLC stopping distance data for MED autobrakes by incorrectly comparing APLC runway data with the landing distance provided on the approach plate for runway 22R

caused_by.evidence: following the accident, FedEx expanded the APLC pilot training presentation for all initial and upgrade training

chain.label: Captain committed to forcing an early touchdown with no float to preserve stopping distance
chain.trigger: he planned to land the airplane at the start of the runway and wanted to ensure that the airplane would not float during the landing flare; 'wasn't going to grease it...but put it on the end of the runway'

caused_by.evidence: the inoperative thrust reverser, the questionable reliability of the autobrake system, and the perceived need to land at the beginning of the runway

the flight crew's calculation error in determining the runway length required for landing influenced the captain's subsequent actions during final approach and landing by creating a sense of urgency to touch down early

chain.label: Captain's overcontrol of the elevator: abrupt nose-down input at 17 feet followed by large, rapid reversals (classic PIO)
chain.trigger: The captain's large and rapid elevator control reversals, which resulted in an increasing divergence above and below the target pitch attitude, were consistent with a 'classic' pilot-induced oscillation (PIO)

caused_by.evidence: the captain's nose-down elevator input at 17 feet radio altitude (2 seconds before the first touchdown) was consistent with an attempt to control the point of touchdown given his concerns about the runway length

chain.label: Destabilized flare, increased sink rate, hard first touchdown and bounce back into the air
chain.trigger: he destabilized the flare and established a greater sink rate... the airplane began to lift off the runway... wing lift was not degraded upon touchdown because the spoilers did not deploy

caused_by.evidence: When the captain rapidly moved the elevators to near neutral instead of maintaining nose-up elevator and continuing the flare (2 seconds before first touchdown), he destabilized the flare

chain.label: Captain did not execute a go-around from the destabilized flare and bounce
chain.trigger: The first officer stated that no attempt was made to execute a go-around... a go-around executed by the captain at any time through the touchdown and bounce would have prevented the accident

caused_by.evidence: A destabilized approach is a compelling reason to initiate an early go-around... If a bounce occurs, a go-around should be initiated

chain.label: Second touchdown on the right main landing gear at 13.5 fps, 0.5 g and 9.5 degrees right-wing-down roll, 3.2 times certification energy
chain.trigger: the accident airplane's right MLG experienced an energy input of 1,574,000 ft-lbs during the second touchdown, which was 3.2 times the maximum certification energy

caused_by.evidence: This large nose-down input, in turn, established a very high sink rate and low g load at the time of the second touchdown. The captain's final, large nose-up inputs were made too late to soften the impact
The airplane touched down for the second time as vertical acceleration was decreasing through 0.5 g
the captain continued to attempt to salvage the landing; however, a go-around executed by the captain at any time through the touchdown and bounce would have prevented the accident

chain.label: Right MLG strut bottomed and right wing rear spar fractured, right gear and wing separated with fuel tank rupture and fire
chain.trigger: the energy transmitted into the right MLG during the second touchdown... was sufficient to fully compress (bottom) the right MLG strut and cause structural failure of the right wing rear spar

caused_by.evidence: the structural failure of the right wing rear spar resulted in the rupture of the right wing fuel tanks and fire

chain.label: Airplane rolled uncontrollably right to inverted while sliding down the runway
chain.trigger: The right-wing-down roll angle increased to 90 degrees... The airplane continued to roll as it slid down the runway

caused_by.evidence: aircraft began to roll clockwise, 'dragging' the right wing underneath; and other failures were consequent

chain.label: Airplane departed the right side of runway 22R and came to rest inverted, destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: coming to rest inverted about 5,126 feet beyond the runway threshold and about 580 feet to the right of the runway centerline... The airplane was destroyed by impact and a postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: runway scrapes, soot marks, and runway surface gouging began turning toward the right of the runway

chain.label: All five occupants received minor injuries in the crash and during egress
chain.trigger: All five occupants received minor injuries in the crash and during subsequent egress through a cockpit window

caused_by.evidence: the airplane came to rest inverted... he released his seat belt and shoulder harness and fell on his head and hand
